items.c: Endometrial endometrioid carcinoma with squamous differentiation and keratin granulomas. H&E stain, high magnification. It shows typical endometrioid adenocarcinoma cells to the left in the image. To the right in the image, separated from the carcinoma cells by a wall of endometrial stroma, is a focus of keratin granuloma. The granuloma contains necrotic “ghost cells” of keratinocytes, leaving eosinophilic keratin as well as clear spaces at the prior locations of the cell nuclei.

items.c: Single cervical biopsy, which was from the 9 o'clock position. It's a no-brainer CIN 3. Moral of the story: Ladies, get those Pap smears annually once you become sexually active! A single negative Pap doesn't mean doodlysquat. Sometimes it takes years for the Pap to pick up a significant premalignant lesion. Also, if you are not getting liquid-based Paps (ThinPrep or SurePath), either you or your doctor is nuts. This case would have never been picked up by a conventional Pap.
